extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature — scientists, members of learned societies, and the wider scientific community
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and administrative standards for scientific societies (meetings, publications, membership, expeditions, and observational practice). Covers how societies should record, publish, examine, and disseminate scientific work and run associated activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership eligibility (Royal Society of Victoria)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘I also wish to remove an impression which, I believe, holds some ground, that advanced scientific attainments are indispensable qualifications for membership. The object for which our Society is founded was the promotion of literature, science, and art in the colony. Whoever can assist in this is, so far, eligible for membership.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership is not restricted to those with advanced scientific attainments; eligibility is framed by the ability to assist in promoting literature, science, and art in the community. (Context: proposal to admit distant residents as country life-members at half subscription.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial sufficiency for publishing Transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘the funds have not been in a sufficiently flourishing condition to enable the council to resume the printing... the only revenue of the Society has been that derived from entrance fees and subscriptions of members... although our income will amply meet these demands if the annual subscriptions of members are regularly paid, there has hitherto been an insufficient sum left to print our Transactions without other aid.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular member subscriptions and/or external aid (e.g., government grant) are required to resume and maintain the regular printing of a society's transactions; fiscal health is a precondition for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic examinations and certification for practical courses
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘It is intended, therefore, at all events to at once print the Transactions... A telegraph class for ladies has also been established ... It is intended ... to hold periodic examinations of the pupils, and to grant certificates to such as prove themselves to be competent.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical teaching programmes should include periodic examinations and the formal granting of certificates contingent on demonstrated competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of observational recording to establish changes in nebulæ
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Several of the drawings which reached home had evidently not been executed with that precision which is so necessary to establish a fact of this kind... No one accustomed to observing could fail to be convinced of change going on, if he only saw the nebulæ with a power of six or seven hundred on the great telescope on good nights at intervals of three or four months... drawings made by Messrs. Le Sueur and Macgeorge... establish the facts beyond all doubt.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To demonstrate real changes in celestial objects one needs precise, careful drawings (or photographs), sufficient resolving power (e.g., 600–700× on the great telescope), repeated observations at multi-month intervals, and high-quality documentation; casual or imprecise sketches are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of photography and timely publication of observational results
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Government has given me authority to publish every month the results of our observations in meteorology, terrestrial magnetism, and of other phenomena... Photography of celestial objects has been commenced with the great telescope, and some exceedingly fine and promising negatives of the moon were taken.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observatory work should be disseminated regularly (monthly) and employ photographic techniques where appropriate; timely publication enhances accessibility and scientific utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for recognition/awards in astronomy
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The Royal Astronomical Society awarded its gold medal this year to Prof. Schiaparelli... principally on account of his researches on the relations that exist between comets and shooting stars.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards recognize significant, original research that establishes important relations or advances understanding of astronomical phenomena (here: linking comets and meteors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Official duty to warn of approaching stormy weather (meteorological responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘It was his duty and in his power to do... they expect from him in future the strictest observance of that portion of his instructions which require him
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities with meteorological responsibilities are expected proactively to furnish notices of approaching stormy weather, to maintain constant vigilance, and to communicate personally when necessary; failure to do so is negligence subject to censure and remedial rule changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption and enforcement of committee safety recommendations (Marine Department)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The Government have ordered the appliances for saving life and property to be considerably increased, and accept in their entirety the recommendations of the Committee, which they resolve to adopt and embody in a code of rules, which will be communicated for the strictest observance by all the departments concerned.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-incident reforms should include concrete measures (increasing life-saving appliances) and a codified set of rules to be strictly observed by all relevant departments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inquiry procedure requiring written categorical answers
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The Society, however, adjourned the inquiry, and have agreed to put their questions in writing, so that Lieutenant Dawson may give them a categorical answer.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal investigations into expedition conduct should seek written, categorical responses to specific questions as part of due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acclimatisation practice for aquarium specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘temporary buildings with the necessary tanks have been provided for the reception of such marine animals and plants as can only be obtained in the summer season. They will then become acclimatised, and the tanks can be afterwards removed to their permanent places in the aquarium.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When establishing an aquarium, use temporary holding tanks to acclimatize seasonally obtained marine specimens before transferring them to permanent exhibits to improve survival and adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition thematic scheduling and division
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Next year’s London International Exhibition will consist of three divisions:—1. Fine Arts; 2. Manufactures; 3. Recent Scientific Inventions and Discoveries of all kinds. We notice that of the future Exhibitions that of 1874 will embrace Artificial Illuminations... 1875.—Hydraulics... 1876.—Photographic Apparatus and Photography... 1877.—Health... 1880.—Chemical Substances and Products...’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International exhibitions plan topical divisions and multi-year thematic foci; exhibitors and organisers should align entries and preparations with the announced division/themes for the given year.
